For K = 32, all stored records have the equal concentration rho, so each new complex beyond 16 evicts the record with the smallest tau, which is the oldest. The last 16 pairs score >= 0.9 and the first 16 score <= 0.15, and overall accuracy is 0.5 ± 0.1. An evicted key and its evicted value both become free, so an evicted key spreads its mass over the roughly 16 freed values. The state holds at most P_max bindings.

complexity.constants_notes: Each fired pulse computes rho in O(r) and touches only the stored records in row i and column j. That is O(P_max) by scan, or O(deg) with row and column index lists. The cached row and column sums are updated in O(1) per changed record. Pruning and the min-concentration eviction cost O(P_max). The readout costs O(V) to form p, the same as any output softmax. Memory is the parameters (2Vr + V + 1), a, the two cached V-arrays of row and column sums, and 4 P_max numbers for the records (i, j, C_ij, tau_ij). Nothing grows with n. Training by BPTT stores the touched records per step.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: One mass-action pulse binds a fraction rho_ij of the free key mass to the demonstrated value. Conservation and the exchange reactions make that binding exclusive and revisable. Pretraining learns only the type-level rate prior.

prediction.metric: In-context exposures per new key-value pair needed to reach top-1 recall >= 0.95 (K = 8 pairs, V = 128 with keys 0-31, values 32-95 and filler 96-127, r = 8, P_max = 64, 1000 held-out sequences with fresh pairings).
prediction.statement: One exposure gives top-1 recall >= 0.95 and mean p(correct) >= 0.9. Secondary prediction: the median over 5 seeds of the number of pretraining sequences (Adam, learning rate 1e-2, batch 32) before held-out one-shot recall first reaches 0.95 is <= 3000. Only 2Vr + V + 1 parameters are trained, and they need only learn that key-value types have rho near 1 while all other type pairs have rho <= kappa.

core_idea: Each demonstrated pair (i, j) fires one pulse of irreversible mass-action reactions: free X_i binds free Y_j, a free X_i displaces other keys from complexes holding Y_j, and a free Y_j displaces other values from complexes holding X_i. The complex concentrations are the memory, so bindings compete through conserved totals and through the order in which they arrived, not through an equilibrium of accumulated counts.

extensions.description: Add the reverse reaction C_ij -> X_i + Y_j with a small learned off-rate applied at each step, which multiplies every entry by (1 - k_off). This gives graceful forgetting on very long streams. The core claims use k_off = 0.
extensions.name: Slow dissociation (forgetting)

extensions.description: Following the continuous-time Markov chain view in W2989086808, replace each deterministic pulse by sampling integer reaction events with the same propensities. At unit counts this gives strict one-to-one bindings.
extensions.name: Finite-count stochastic pulses

extensions.description: Replace the unit totals a_i with learned per-type capacities, so that function words can bind several successors. The conservation-based x and y then use the capacities in place of a.

equations.latex: x_i = s^L_i a_i - \sum_l C_{il},\quad y_j = s^R_j a_j - \sum_m C_{mj}
equations.plain: x[i] = sL[i]*a[i] - rowsum_i(C); y[j] = sR[j]*a[j] - colsum_j(C)

extensions.name: Learned capacities

On ownership transfer (q a r a, then query q), the trained model gives p(a|q) >= 0.5 while p(a|r) >= 0.9. Exchange would then not be releasing displaced keys.

After pretraining, more than 5% of filler-filler type pairs keep rho > kappa, or recall accuracy with L = 4000 fillers falls by more than 0.02 from L = 0. Either would show that the unpredictable-successor gradient does not close the gate.

known_relatives.claimed_difference: In a count cache, cell (i,j) changes only when (i,j) is shown, by a state-independent increment, and writes commute. Here a pulse on (i,j) rescales every entry in row i and column j by factors that depend on the current free masses x_i and y_j, and the increment to C_ij is quadratic in the state. So cells that are not shown at step t change, and the order of writes matters beyond any decay.
known_relatives.name: Linear attention / one-hot count cache (Transformers are RNNs)
known_relatives.relation: Both keep a V x V type-indexed memory written when a pair is shown.

known_relatives.claimed_difference: The delta rule only touches row i, with beta_t a function of the input. Here column j is also rescaled by (1 - rho x_i), where x_i = a_i - sum_l C_il is a function of the state. A committed key therefore cannot steal a value, and a free key can. The resulting recursion is quadratic in C, while the delta rule's is linear.
known_relatives.name: Delta rule / gated DeltaNet
known_relatives.relation: With one-hot keys, the delta rule decays row i and writes cell (i,j), which resembles value-side exchange.

known_relatives.claimed_difference: There is no matrix scaling and no equilibrium. The memory is the trajectory of irreversible kinetics and does not lie on the toric variety of any per-cell kernel. Its 2x2 cross-ratios depend on demonstrations of other cells and on their order (capability 4).
known_relatives.name: Sinkhorn / OT attention with dustbin (Sinkformer, SuperGlue) and pointer-sentinel mixtures
known_relatives.relation: The parent card reduced to this family. The readout also mixes a bound part with a background.

known_relatives.claimed_difference: There is no learned recurrent matrix and no elementwise nonlinearity f(W h + U x). The recurrence is the mass-action map of a fixed set of three elementary reactions. It is sparse in the support of the state, preserves the stoichiometric totals exactly and keeps the state nonnegative. The only learned part is the type-level rate prior.
known_relatives.name: Nonlinear RNNs and multiplicative RNNs
known_relatives.relation: Any state-dependent recurrence is an RNN in the broad sense.

learning.description: E_raw, F_raw, l and c are trained by next-token cross-entropy with backpropagation through time over the pulse recursion. Each fired pulse is a polynomial map of C and rho_ij, so gradients flow through C and, through rho_ij, into E and F (d rho / d k = 1/(1+k)^2). The discrete parts are handled as follows. (1) Gate: the indicator 1[rho > kappa] is computed without gradient. When it is 1, the pulse is in the graph and rho receives gradient. When it is 0, the step is the identity and that rho receives no gradient from that step. (2) Pruning and eviction: the set of deleted records is computed without gradient (stop-gradient on the comparison and on the argmin), and deletion is applied as multiplication of those entries by a constant 0 mask. Deleted entries pass zero gradient, and surviving entries pass gradient unchanged. (3) Readout: differentiable in C, l and c. Pretraining uses synthetic binding sequences with fresh random pairings, value->key transitions to random fresh keys, and runs of filler tokens (96-127) at random positions whose successors are uniformly random. So no binding is ever stored in weights. How the filler and bridge rates fall below kappa: if a pair (f, f') or (v, k) whose successor is unpredictable fires with rho > kappa, it binds X_f to Y_f', which raises C[f,f'] in f's readout and lowers its free mass. The next time f appears with a different random successor, the loss at that token increases with C[f,f']. The gradient on rho_{ff'} is therefore positive in the loss until rho falls below kappa, and then the gate closes. Key->value rates rise toward 1 because the value after a demonstrated key at query time is predicted by C[key, value]. Nothing is updated by gradient at test time.

equations.name: training loss
equations.plain: loss = - sum over t of log p_t[w_{t+1}], backpropagated through the sequence of pulses, with gate and deletion masks held constant.

equations.name: masked deletion in the backward pass
equations.plain: After each pulse: M[e] = 0 for records deleted by pruning or eviction and 1 otherwise, computed without gradient. C = M * C.

learning.few_shot_argument: Take a fresh pair (i, j) with x_i = y_j = 1 and no competitors. One pulse sets C_ij = rho_ij. The readout of key i then puts mass at least rho_ij on j, so one demonstration is enough once pretraining has driven rho to about 0.95 for key-value types. Overwriting also takes one shot: after (q,a), the pulse for (q,b) gives C_qb = rho and C_qa = rho(1-rho). Ownership transfer takes one shot: after (q,a) and then (r,a), C_ra = rho and C_qa = rho(1-rho), so q is released and its free mass is routed to values that are still free. Elimination comes from conservation. A key that was never demonstrated routes all its mass by u ⊙ (y + eta), and every demonstrated value has y = 1 - rho or less, so the one value left free in the inventory takes most of the probability. All of these follow from the conserved stoichiometry and the mass-action pulse. There is no lookup and no gradient step.

readout.latex: p_t(v) = C_t[q,v] + x_q\,\frac{u_v\,(y_v + \eta)}{\sum_{v'} u_{v'}(y_{v'} + \eta)},\quad q = w_t
readout.name: bound row plus free mass routed to available values
readout.plain: Runs last at step t, after steps 1-5. q = w_t. x_q = a[q] - sum_v C[q,v]. y = a - column sums of C. g = u*(y+eta); g = g/sum(g). p[v] = C[q,v] + x_q*g[v]. Because a[q] = 1, sum_v p[v] = sum_v C[q,v] + x_q = 1 exactly.

state.meaning: V is the vocabulary size and r is the rank of the rate prior. E = Theta[:, :r] and F = Theta[:, r:] are each V x r. The rate constant for left species X_i meeting right species Y_j is k_ij = E_i . F_j, and the pulse extent is rho_ij = k_ij / (1 + k_ij), which lies in [0, 1). E_raw and F_raw are initialized so that every k_ij is about 1 (rho about 0.5, above the gate kappa), so every type pair starts out reacting and receives gradient. This prior encodes which token types react, for example keys with values. It never stores a binding.
state.name: Theta = [E | F]
state.type: learned parameter block, nonnegative (E = softplus(E_raw), F = softplus(F_raw))

state.meaning: u = softmax(l) is the background distribution over the V tokens. It is used only to route a key's free mass in the readout.
state.name: l

state.meaning: eta = softplus(c) > 0 is the availability floor used when routing free key mass. It keeps the routing denominator positive and gives tokens not present in context a small share.
state.name: c

state.meaning: a_t[i] = 1 if token i has occurred in w_1..w_t, else 0, with a_0 = 0. It is the conserved total of both X_i and Y_i.
state.name: a_t

state.meaning: C_t[i,j] is the concentration of complex C_ij = X_i:Y_j. All indexing (C_t[i,j], rows, columns, row and column sums) refers to this V x V matrix, and entries not stored are 0. It is stored as a list of at most P_max records (i, j, C_t[i,j], tau_ij), where tau_ij is the step of the last pulse that wrote cell (i,j). tau is used only to break ties in eviction. P_max is a fixed capacity independent of n. Free amounts are derived through conservation rather than stored: x_i = a_t[i] - sum_l C_t[i,l] and y_j = a_t[j] - sum_m C_t[m,j]. Implementations cache the row sums and column sums as two V-arrays and update them whenever an entry changes. C_0 = 0 (no records).
state.name: C_t (complex matrix)
state.type: sparse nonnegative V x V matrix with at most P_max nonzero entries

update.name: species injection (step 1 of t)
update.plain: if a[w_t] == 0: a[w_t] = 1. The new X and Y mass enters free, because no entry of C involves w_t yet. This runs first at every t.

update.latex: i = w_{t-1},\; j = w_t,\; \rho = \frac{E_i^{\top}F_j}{1 + E_i^{\top}F_j},\; \text{fire iff } t \ge 2 \text{ and } \rho > \kappa
update.name: pulse extent and gate (step 2 of t)
update.plain: i = w[t-1]; j = w[t]; k = dot(E[i], F[j]); rho = k/(1+k). The pulse fires only if t >= 2 and rho > kappa, with kappa = 1e-3 fixed. If it does not fire, steps 3-5 are skipped entirely: C_t = C_{t-1}, no tau changes, nothing is pruned or evicted, and the readout at t uses C_t = C_{t-1} with the updated a_t.

update.latex: x_i = a_i - \sum_l C_{il},\; y_j = a_j - \sum_m C_{mj},\; \mathrm{row}_i = \sum_{l \ne j} C_{il},\; \mathrm{col}_j = \sum_{m \ne i} C_{mj}
update.name: pre-pulse free masses and competitors (step 3 of t, only if fired)
update.plain: All four quantities are computed from C_{t-1} (with a_t) before any entry is changed. C_{t-1} is the matrix left after step 5 of the previous fired step, so it already reflects all earlier pruning and eviction. row_i is X_i mass already bound to other values. col_j is Y_j mass already bound to other keys.

update.latex: C_{ij} \mathrel{+}= \rho\,(x_i y_j + x_i\,\mathrm{col}_j + y_j\,\mathrm{row}_i);\quad C_{mj} \mathrel{*}= (1 - \rho x_i)\;(m \ne i);\quad C_{il} \mathrel{*}= (1 - \rho y_j)\;(l \ne j)
update.name: mass-action pulse: binding plus two strand-exchange reactions (step 4 of t, only if fired)
update.plain: Using the pre-pulse values: C[i,j] += rho*(x_i*y_j + x_i*col_j + y_j*row_i). For every stored entry (m,j) with m != i: C[m,j] *= (1 - rho*x_i), because X_i displaces X_m and X_m is released. For every stored entry (i,l) with l != j: C[i,l] *= (1 - rho*y_j), because Y_j displaces Y_l and Y_l is released. Create the record (i,j) if it is absent, and set tau_ij = t. Mass is conserved exactly. New x_i = x_i(1 - rho(y_j + col_j)) >= 0 and new y_j = y_j(1 - rho(x_i + row_i)) >= 0. Released X_m and Y_l become free.

update.name: finite volume: pruning, then eviction (step 5 of t, only if fired)
update.plain: Runs immediately after step 4 and before the readout at t, so the readout at t and step 3 at the next fired step both see the pruned matrix. First delete every record with C < eps (eps = 1e-4). Then, while more than P_max records remain, delete the record with the smallest concentration, breaking ties by the smallest tau (the oldest pulse). A pulse creates at most one record, so this deletes at most one record per step. Deleting a record returns its mass to the free pools through conservation. The cached row and column sums are updated.

non_reduction_argument.broken_invariant: The parent's mapping relied on two properties. (1) The state is a count matrix N in which cell (i,j) changes only when pair (i,j) is shown, by an increment that does not depend on the state. The state is therefore a commutative sum of one-hot outer-product writes. (2) The readout is a scaling of a kernel K_ij = f(history of cell (i,j)), so the plan lies on the toric variety: every 2x2 cross-ratio P_ij P_kl / (P_il P_kj) equals K_ij K_kl / (K_il K_kj) and depends only on those four cells' own histories. The pulse (update step 4) breaks both properties. The increment to C_ij is rho(x_i y_j + x_i col_j + y_j row_i), where x_i, y_j, row_i and col_j are linear in C, so the recursion is quadratic in the state. The same pulse rescales every entry (m,j) by (1 - rho x_i) and every entry (i,l) by (1 - rho y_j), so cells change when other cells are shown. In the toy example the block cells (0,3), (0,4), (1,3) and (1,4) have identical write histories in streams A and B, yet their cross-ratio is 1.7277 in A and 1.0514 in B.
non_reduction_argument.known_family: other_known: gated one-hot outer-product count cache (linear attention / bigram cache, LFU-capped) read through unbalanced Sinkhorn normalization with a dustbin and a pointer-sentinel mix
non_reduction_argument.why_unrepairable: Strongest repair: Sinkhorn or equilibrium scaling of a kernel K_ij = f_theta(times and counts of the writes to cell (i,j)), with any learned f (decay, recency, saturation) and any marginals or dustbin. Whatever f is, the cross-ratio of a 2x2 block is fixed by the four cells' histories, so it must agree on streams A and B, and our state does not. Second repair: a gated delta rule with one-hot keys. It modifies only row i, with beta_t depending on the input. Matching us would need a column-j rescaling by (1 - rho x_i), with x_i = 1 - sum_l C_il read from the state, and that makes the recursion nonlinear in S. Third repair: a two-sided linear update S <- A_t S B_t + W_t with input-dependent A_t and B_t. It is linear in S (vec(S) evolves by B_t^T ⊗ A_t), so it cannot produce factors and increments that are products of state entries. A larger lifted state could hold monomials of C, but the pulse generates higher-degree products at every step, so no finite fixed lift closes. What remains is the generic catch-all of a nonlinear RNN. The card concedes that class, but its member here is a fixed, parameter-free mass-action map that conserves stoichiometry, not f(W h + U x).

references.why: This paper models a reaction system through mass-action propensity functions over a sparse set of candidate reactions, learned with l1 sparsity. I take the mass-action propensity law for elementary bimolecular reactions (rate = k times the product of reactant amounts) and the sparse reaction support. The context switches reactions on, and the rates come from a learned low-rank type prior.

This paper identifies a small set of influential reactions and builds a reduced mechanism from them. I use the same idea in the finite volume: only P_max complex species and their reactions are kept, and the weakest are dissolved.

source_transplant.change: Reactions do not run continuously. A reaction fires as one unit pulse (one explicit step of the rate equations) only when the context presents its pair. The rates come from a learned low-rank type prior and saturate as rho = k/(1+k). The set of complex species is capped at P_max, and the weakest complexes are dissolved. The current token's bound row and free fraction are read out as a next-token distribution.
source_transplant.object: Mass-action kinetics of elementary bimolecular reactions with stoichiometric conservation: binding X_i + Y_j -> C_ij and the exchange reactions X_i + C_mj -> C_ij + X_m and Y_j + C_il -> C_ij + Y_l, each with propensity k times the product of reactant concentrations, over a sparse reaction support.

summary:
Tokens are chemical species. When token i first appears, one unit of a left species X_i and one unit of a right species Y_i enter the volume, both free. The memory is a sparse V x V matrix of complex concentrations C_ij with at most P_max nonzero entries. Free amounts follow from conservation: x_i = a_i - sum_l C_il and y_j = a_j - sum_m C_mj.

When the adjacent pair (w_{t-1}, w_t) = (i, j) has a learned rate rho_ij above a threshold, it fires one pulse of three bimolecular mass-action reactions at that rate:
- binding: X_i + Y_j -> C_ij;
- key-side exchange: X_i + C_mj -> C_ij + X_m;
- value-side exchange: Y_j + C_il -> C_ij + Y_l.

The pulse adds rho (x_i y_j + x_i col_j + y_j row_i) to C_ij. It multiplies every other entry in column j by (1 - rho x_i) and every other entry in row i by (1 - rho y_j). The update is quadratic in the state. A cell changes when a different cell is demonstrated, and the size of the change depends on how much free mass the rest of the network has left. The memory is therefore not a sum of per-pair writes, and it is not the equilibrium of any kernel built from per-pair histories.

Each step runs in a fixed order: injection, gate, pulse (if gated on), finite-volume pruning and eviction, then readout. The readout for the current token q is its bound row C_q plus its free fraction x_q, and the free fraction is routed to a background u reweighted by the free value mass y. This gives one-shot recall, one-shot overwrite, ownership transfer (a key whose value is taken by another key is released) and elimination toward values that are still free. Cost per token is O(V + P_max), independent of n.
title: Strand-Exchange Binding Kinetics: in-context bindings as irreversible mass-action binding and displacement pulses under conservation laws

toy_example.description: Keys 0, 1, 2 and values 3, 4, 5. E and F make k = 1 (so rho = 0.5) for every key->value pair and k = 0 for every other pair, so value->key bridges are gated out. Both streams share the prefix 0 3 1 4 0 4 1 3, which demonstrates all four cells of the 2x2 block {0,1} x {3,4}. Stream A appends 2 3 0 3 and stream B appends 2 5 0 3. The four block cells have identical write histories in A and B, so a per-cell-kernel Sinkhorn model would give equal cross-ratios. The pulses give 1.7277 and 1.0514. P_max = 16 is never reached, so eviction does not trigger. The script also prints key 0's free fraction and its readout over values in B, using u uniform over values and eta = 0 as a limiting case.
toy_example.python:
import json
import numpy as np
V = 6
E = np.array([1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0], dtype=float)
F = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], dtype=float)
kappa, eps, Pmax = 1e-3, 1e-4, 16
u = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], dtype=float) / 3.0
eta = 0.0
def run(seq):
    a = np.zeros(V)
    C = {}
    prev = None
    for w in seq:
        if a[w] == 0:
            a[w] = 1.0
        if prev is not None:
            k = E[prev] * F[w]
            rho = k / (1.0 + k)
            if rho > kappa:
                i, j = prev, w
                xi = a[i] - sum(c for (p, q), c in C.items() if p == i)
                yj = a[j] - sum(c for (p, q), c in C.items() if q == j)
                col = sum(c for (p, q), c in C.items() if q == j and p != i)
                row = sum(c for (p, q), c in C.items() if p == i and q != j)
                cij = C.get((i, j), 0.0)
                new = {}
                for (p, q), c in C.items():
                    if (p, q) == (i, j):
                        continue
                    if q == j:
                        new[(p, q)] = c * (1.0 - rho * xi)
                    elif p == i:
                        new[(p, q)] = c * (1.0 - rho * yj)
                    else:
                        new[(p, q)] = c
                new[(i, j)] = cij + rho * (xi * yj + xi * col + yj * row)
                new = {kk: c for kk, c in new.items() if c >= eps}
                while len(new) > Pmax:
                    kmin = min(new, key=lambda z: new[z])
                    del new[kmin]
                C = new
        prev = w
    return a, C
def cross(C):
    return C[(0, 3)] * C[(1, 4)] / (C[(0, 4)] * C[(1, 3)])
def readout(a, C, q):
    Cq = np.zeros(V)
    colsum = np.zeros(V)
    for (p, s), c in C.items():
        colsum[s] += c
        if p == q:
            Cq[s] += c
    xq = a[q] - Cq.sum()
    y = a - colsum
    g = u * (y + eta)
    g = g / g.sum()
    return Cq + xq * g, xq
prefix = [0, 3, 1, 4, 0, 4, 1, 3]
seqA = prefix + [2, 3, 0, 3]
seqB = prefix + [2, 5, 0, 3]
_, Cp = run(prefix)
aA, CA = run(seqA)
aB, CB = run(seqB)
pA, x0A = readout(aA, CA, 0)
pB, x0B = readout(aB, CB, 0)
out = {
    "cr_prefix": round(float(cross(Cp)), 4),
    "cr_A": round(float(cross(CA)), 4),
    "cr_B": round(float(cross(CB)), 4),
    "x0_A": round(float(x0A), 4),
    "x0_B": round(float(x0B), 4),
    "p_q0_B_values": [round(float(t), 4) for t in pB[3:]],
    "mass_q0_B": round(float(pB.sum()), 4)
}
print(json.dumps(out))
